articleTitle: A system that monitors whether or not tyres on wheeled vehicles are under or over inflated which may be further developed to measure tyre pressures. This system may then in turn be used to detect overloaded axles
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Tyre Monitoring (Digest No. 1997/046)
abstract: Traffic 2000 Ltd. have become world leaders in piezo electric technology for the traffic industry. We have devised various types of piezoelectric detectors that have led to the design of a tyre monitoring system. We are able to measure speed very accurately indeed in free flowing traffic, axle passage from 0 to 150 mph and width of wheels. We are able to monitor bicycle passage in mixed traffic roads, differentiate between bicycle, motorbikes, cars, and all manner of commercial vehicles.

articleTitle: Tyre pressure, damper condition and wheel balance assessment from vibration measurements
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Tyre Monitoring (Digest No. 1997/046)
abstract: The work reported shows the possibility of informing drivers when attention to tyre pressure, damper and wheel balance is required. The proposed system offers a number of advantages: no invasion of the tyre air space; it can be retrofitted, suitable transducers are being fitted for use in advanced suspension systems so the necessary raw signal could be obtained very cheaply; the cost of accelerometers for this type of application are falling rapidly. The main disadvantage of the proposed system would be the need to provide calibration facility to accommodate any change in tyre size. This is not considered to be a serious problem as further research will be able to establish the range of calibration factors and onboard software could easily accommodate this potential variable. Adoption of such a system is considered to provide increased safety and a reduction in operating and maintenance costs for the motorist.

articleTitle: Low cost tyre monitoring system using electronic article surveillance techniques
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Tyre Monitoring (Digest No. 1997/046)
abstract: A low cost method for tyre monitoring has been outlined. This method is contactless and relies on a passive LC circuit whose properties can be made to change with tyre pressure, responding to a burst of RF energy. Preliminary experimental work has verified the principles of the system and its ability to detect changes of circuit performance. The simple nature of the passive LC circuit could make it suitable for incorporation into a tyre sidewall or tyre valve.
